children: to Outperform from In-Line on Monday, citing the shopping mall REIT's improved balance sheet, accelerating FFO growth, and reduced leverage profile.

"MAC continues to see good momentum in their portfolio, with commentary at a recent investor conference noting that ’26 renewals are complete, with MAC working on deals in ’27 and beyond," Evercore ISI analyst Steve Sakwa wrote in a note to clients.

The leasing part of the company's Path Forward plan is largely complete. That puts the focus on those tenants opening and paying rent, he said. Evercore now expects the signed, not open, pipeline to boost leased occupancy to 96.1% by the end of 2028.

Macerich's forward equity raise and convertible bond issuance are also adding to Evercore ISI's estimate, giving the company the ability to repay higher coupon debt or to deploy into new investments at high single-digit going-in yields, stabilizing in the low double digits. Regarding the balance sheet, leverage is expected to fall to ~6.0x net debt/EBITDA, down from ~9.0x pre-Path Forward, the analyst said.
"Mall fundamentals continue to improve, with solid retailer demand and shrinking supply giving established landlords greater pricing power," Sakwa said.

title: Macerich upgraded to Outperform at Evercore ISI as Path Forward progresses
